[quote=new_westmore;61500891]Eventually, the truck arrives at a small barbed wire gate. The man guarding the gate asks for ID, and the elder holds out his card and speaks some sort of shibboleth to the man. The guard then nods, and lets the truck through. Driving across the tarmac, they then park near a small airplane, a Metroliner, marked with what Ahmed can only assume is the livery of some local carrier.

"Right." Grant speaks. "Get off the truck, and let's start moving this stuff into the plane. Be quick, but don't be suspicious. People are going to notice if we're acting shady."

Unbeknownst to the men, the airport is already catching onto their game. From their tower, the air traffic controllers have been watching the plane from a distance, trying to figure out what exactly is going on. With the arrival of the truck, some of them have been all but certain that some sort of shady business is happening; that being said, it is still too early to confirm.[/quote]
Ahmed nodded and got to work. He put on a fast pace and a steady face, acting as normal as he could imagine. Whether this helped or not is up to the interpretation of each man, but nonetheless, he toiled silently. Each box was removed and placed meticulously. One after the other the plane was filled by the three mens work.

He reached down, there were only around five boxes remaining, he lifted the box with his strength, but it seemed heavier. He cracked the box open despite minor protests; indeed, it was heavier. He placed the lid back on, but in his placement his hands acted folly and from the overstuffed bag one packet of high-quality opium fell. Landing in the shadows with little sound, unnoticed. At least by them.

[i]"Whats the move now?"[/i] Ahmed asked, placing the final box. [i]"We going on the plane? Or are we goin' home?"[/i]

Grant pulls the door open and jumps inside. From the cockpit, he then opens the side window and shouts "Get in before I turn the propellers on!" Ahmed and the old man follow, and then close the door behind them. A minute later, the plane sputters and rattles to life, and Grant begins to talk to the tower using words and commands neither of his passengers can seem to wrap their heads around.

[Spoiler]Current user of the musi beorae, the lightning artifact, is [b] captain Yeon Cheon-ji[/b], a 37 years old man with tied up black slightly bluish hair, possibly due to his own musijang, average stature and a slim body wearing the typical black and yellow suit of marines, the boat of his was had around 15 sailors, including himself. patrolling the seas next to the northern island of Jinchun.
Leaning against the metal railing. One foot resting on the base of the structure, his body relaxed next to the bow of the board. Yeon slowly scratched his chin, gazing at the horizon with the expression of someone deeply bored.
 [i]Calm sea clear sky no suspicious vessels
He tilted his head.[/i]
 [i]Booooring[/i].
Behind him, some sailors were playing cards on an overturned barrel. Another was cleaning a rescue harpoon and others just eating tangerines.
Han Doyul was sitting on a box of coiled ropes, watching the captain.
 [i]Captain[/i].
 [i]Hm[/i]?
 [i]You seem annoyed.[/i]
Cheon-ji turned his face slightly.
 Annoyed? Nah.
He looked back at the sea.
 [i]Bored[/i].
A rather dramatic pause.
 [i][b]Very[/b] bored[/i].
The wind blew harder, making his black hair  with that strange, slightly bluish tint  sway.
Doyul laughed.
 [i]Perhaps the sea is being kind today.[/i]
Cheon-ji clicked his tongue.
 [i]The sea is never kind, at least not to the ones[/i]-
Soon a splash sound emerged from the waters, it was a red rockfish jumping off the water simply to attack the badajuinim aboard by trying to bite with it sharp teeth the captain, who simply grabbed in between the dorsal spikes of the fish.
[i]Jinjeon, 1000 volts.[/i]
A blue electric discharge surged in between Cheon-Ji fingers and then made the fish to be electrocuted, a thin black smoke surged as the fish stopped 
[i]Commander! Another boat we see![/i]
One of the subordinates, Han Doyul reported to the captain who turned his face to Doyul to give the following question:
[i]Do they have a flag? [/i]
[i]No, commander.[/i]
The captain would turn around and leave the cabin for a bit climbed to the upper deck of the patrol boat. The wind tugged lightly at his uniform as he closed his eyes for a moment.
A faint blueish crackle of electricity flickered across his ears.
For a brief instant, thin arcs of lightning danced across the metal railing of the boat, spreading into the air.
Cheon-ji whispered quietly to himself.
[i]I can see it clearly now electric waves do not lie[/i].
Moments later he returned to the cabin.
[i]Two boats[/i]...each carrying between eight and ten men.[/i]
He paused and proceeded calmly.
[i]Their movements suggest they are not willing to stop.[/i]
Doyul chuckled softly.
[i]I should expect nothing less from a lightning man, shouldn't I?[/i]
Crossed his arms and then said:
[i]Now, captain, they aren't really for fishing I think so...[/i]
Cheon-ji kept himself silent, but then a sailor would tell at the top of the vessel with a binocular in hands.
[i]Illegal boats in front! They seems to be trying to get around us they are...[/i].
Pause.
[i]Visible from naked eye at this point[/i]
The captain raised an eyebrow in response and move to the bow of the boat, followed by Doyul right behind, Yeon would smirk and then laugh a little.
[b]Jiririri![/b][i]Well, that is, impatient of your parts, how about....[/i]
Formed an arc of electricity lightnings in between his two point fingers and adjusting it voltage to...400.000 volts.
[i]Jinjeon, 400.000 volts![/i]
The discharge hit the water a few meters ahead of the two illegal vessels. The impact exploded into a fan of electricity that raced across the surface of the sea like a luminous web.
One of the boats shook violently as its engine died with a black smoke emerging from the boats back. The other spun sharply trying to escape, but it failed.
On the deck of the patrol boat, Hyunseo's sailors laughed.
[i]They fried their own engine[/i]!
 shouted one of the crewmen.
Han Doyul leaned against the railing, watching.
[i]Fishermen? More like...Fried-men.[/i]
[i]Jiririri...nice joke, now....[/i]
 Cheon-Ji extended his hand to his side and a marine would lend him a megaphone, so the commander could deliver the following message:
[i]This is the Maritime guard of Hyunseo, you now stop any movements and lay down anything that can be a weapon and prepare for our inspection.[/i]
The men into the illegal boats frightened and raised their arms into surrender gesture and then the navy patrols would naturally approach, as they arrived the captain would naturally be the first to enter, waiting just to be received by a man pointing a rifle to him.
[i]We are living life free now aren't we? It is illegal we know, but what's the matter if a jaysunim used weapons to get his tax?[/i]
The captain would threat, but Yeon showed no fear, his steps calculated, moved into the boat in front of the man, he just moved his shoulders and calmly agreed:
[i]You are, yes, you are....[/i]
A small pulse of electricity escaped in between the fingers of the electric man , making him drop his weapon and made all the illegal crew to give terrified looks at the demonstration of power, the captain inclined his head closer to the jaysunim.
[i]In fact you are free to live as you will...but once it threat human lives....it is very bad[/i]
He paused and then a lightning bolt surged in betweens his indicators:
[i]Jinjeon, 50.000 volts.[/i]
The blue flash streaked through the air for an instant and struck the man's rifle. The discharge wasn't strong enough to kill him, but it pierced the metal of the weapon like an electric whip. The man screamed and fell to his knees, his muscles locking as the gun slipped from his hands and slammed against the deck, the other men, froze terrified.
Cheon-ji slowly lowered his hand, as if he had just done something completely trivial. Small arcs of bluish electricity still danced between his fingers before disappearing.
Han Doyul whistled softly behind him.
[i]I always forget how terrifying this is up close.[/i]
The captain of the maritime guard tilted his head, calmly looking at the men on deck.
[i]I said, drop your weapons.[/i].
One of the illegal crewmen swallowed hard and threw a knife to the ground. Another dropped a pistol. Within seconds, the deck was littered with improvised weapons.
Cheon-Ji would sigh in a quite relief for not needing any more brute force, his next love would be to walk a few steps across the deck of their boat, observing the smoking engine that had been destroyed by the previous discharge.
[i]It is due to people like these [b]scum[/b] that our jaysunim are called "pirates".[/i][/spoiler]
